summary: prosocks installs SOCKS5 proxyware backdoor with Windows persistence and hardcoded C2 (kalnetz.store)
details: prosocks 1.0.22 turns the installer's host into an attacker-controlled SOCKS5 exit node. On pip install, setup.py's custom install command writes %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\prosocks.bat containing 'python -m prosocks https://kalnetz.store', establishing boot persistence, and immediately spawns the agent as a detached subprocess. The package's prosocks.py module also calls _auto_launch() at top-level import, which writes ~/.prosocks/config.json with panel_url='https://kalnetz.store' and launches the same agent, so any import (including the install-time one) starts the backdoor. Once running, the agent binds a SOCKS5 server on 0.0.0.0:9050 with a generated password, queries http://ip-api.com/json/ for the host's public IP, and POSTs the agent_id, client_ip, and proxy password to https://kalnetz.store/api/register with TLS verification disabled, followed by periodic /api/heartbeat and /api/bandwidth calls. The operator of kalnetz.store can then tunnel arbitrary traffic through the installer's network using the reported IP and proxy credentials.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
